column1: # released-binary-digests.tsv — the digest of every published testbucket
# WHY IT EXISTS. For an exact release tag the installer downloads the platform
# archive and `checksums.txt` FROM THE SAME RELEASE and verifies one against
# the other. Both are release assets, `gh release upload --clobber` can replace
# them together, and the Releases API reports every current testbucket release
# as `immutable: false` — so an actor able to publish assets can replace the
# archive and its checksum in one step and the installer's check still passes.
# A tag name is metadata; that check authenticated an archive against metadata
# This file is the root outside the release. It lives in the repository, so it
# is covered by review and by branch protection rather than by the release
# asset store, and the installer refuses any released binary whose bytes do not
# match the line for its exact tag and platform.
# WHAT IT PROVES, EXACTLY. Each line pins the bytes as published at the moment
# the line was committed. It does not, by itself, say those bytes are the ones
# built from the reviewed tip — the build attestation in the Stage-1 manifest
# is what says that, and it is verified separately. What this closes is the
# replacement: bytes swapped after the line was reviewed no longer install.
# binary INSIDE the archive — not of the archive. The archive digest says which
# archive was downloaded; this says which binary is about to execute, which is
# ADDING A RELEASE. Publish, then compute the digest of the extracted binary
